title: Principles of Accounting
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 100L second-semester Principles of Accounting curriculum, building on introductory financial accounting: single entry and incomplete records, control accounts, manufacturing accounts, accounts of non-trading (non-profit) organizations, partnership fundamentals, and departmental/joint venture accounts basics.

questions.question: A business that keeps records under the single entry system typically maintains complete records for which of the following?
options: All debit and credit aspects of every transaction
questions.explanation: Single entry (incomplete records) usually keeps a cash book and personal accounts but not a full double-entry system for every transaction.

questions.question: Under the statement of affairs method, opening capital is calculated as:
questions.explanation: A statement of affairs is a balance-sheet-style listing used to derive capital (assets minus liabilities) at a point in time when full records are not kept.

questions.question: A trader's capital at the start of the year was N450,000 and at the end was N610,000. During the year drawings were N80,000 and no additional capital was introduced. What was the profit for the year?
questions.explanation: Profit = (Closing capital + Drawings) - (Opening capital + Additional capital) = (610,000 + 80,000) - 450,000 = 240,000.

questions.question: In incomplete records, if additional capital of N50,000 was introduced during the year, opening capital was N200,000, closing capital was N260,000, and drawings were N30,000, what is the profit or loss for the year?
A sales ledger control account is used mainly to:
options: Verify the arithmetical accuracy of the individual debtors' accounts
Replace the need for a sales day book
questions.correct_answer: Verify the arithmetical accuracy of the individual debtors' accounts
questions.explanation: A control account totals postings to individual ledger accounts and its balance should agree with the sum of individual debtor balances, acting as a check.

questions.question: Which of the following would appear on the credit side of a sales ledger (debtors) control account?
options: Cash and cheques received from debtors
questions.correct_answer: Cash and cheques received from debtors
questions.explanation: Cash/cheque receipts from debtors reduce the amount they owe, so they are credited to the control account.

questions.question: Opening debtors were N120,000, credit sales for the period were N500,000, cash received from debtors was N430,000, and discounts allowed were N15,000. What is the closing debtors balance?
In a purchases ledger (creditors) control account, returns outward (purchase returns) are recorded on which side?
questions.explanation: Returns outward reduce the amount owed to suppliers, so they are debited to the purchases ledger control account.

questions.question: The main purpose of preparing a manufacturing account is to determine the:
options: Production cost of goods completed during the period
questions.correct_answer: Production cost of goods completed during the period
questions.explanation: A manufacturing account computes the cost of manufacturing (production cost) of goods completed, which is then transferred to the trading account.

questions.question: In a manufacturing account, 'prime cost' consists of:
options: Direct materials + direct labour + direct expenses
Direct materials + direct labour + factory overheads
questions.correct_answer: Direct materials + direct labour + direct expenses
questions.explanation: Prime cost is the sum of all direct costs: direct materials, direct labour, and direct expenses, before factory overheads are added.

questions.question: Direct materials consumed = Opening stock of raw materials + Purchases of raw materials - ____.
questions.explanation: Materials consumed is found by adjusting purchases for opening and closing raw material stock: Opening stock + Purchases - Closing stock.

questions.question: A manufacturer had opening raw materials stock of N60,000, purchased raw materials worth N320,000, and had closing raw materials stock of N45,000. What is the cost of raw materials consumed?
Where work-in-progress exists, the production cost of goods completed is prime cost plus factory overheads, adjusted by:
options: Opening stock of finished goods only
questions.explanation: Opening WIP is added and closing WIP is subtracted to arrive at the cost of production of goods actually completed in the period.

questions.question: In accounts of non-trading (non-profit) organizations, the equivalent of a trading and profit and loss account is called the:
questions.explanation: The income and expenditure account is prepared on the accruals basis to show the surplus or deficit of a non-profit organization, analogous to a profit and loss account.

questions.question: A receipts and payments account is best described as a summary of:
options: All cash and bank transactions during the period, regardless of the period they relate to
Only income accrued during the period
Only expenses accrued during the period
questions.correct_answer: All cash and bank transactions during the period, regardless of the period they relate to
questions.explanation: A receipts and payments account is simply a summarized cash book, recording actual cash received and paid without adjusting for accruals or prepayments.

questions.question: In non-profit accounting, the excess of income over expenditure is called a:
questions.explanation: Because non-profit organizations do not earn 'profit' for owners, the excess of income over expenditure is termed a surplus (or deficit if expenditure exceeds income).

questions.question: For a sports club, subscriptions received in advance during the current year should be treated as:
options: A liability in the balance sheet, not income of the current year
Income of the current year in full
An asset in the balance sheet
questions.correct_answer: A liability in the balance sheet, not income of the current year
questions.explanation: Subscriptions received in advance relate to a future period, so they are a liability (owed back in service, not yet earned) rather than current year income.

questions.question: A club received N250,000 in subscriptions during the year. Subscriptions in arrears at the start were N20,000 and at the end were N15,000; subscriptions received in advance at the start were N10,000 and at the end were N25,000. What is the subscription income for the income and expenditure account?
questions.explanation: Income = Cash received - Opening arrears + Closing arrears + Opening advance - Closing advance = 250,000 - 20,000 + 15,000 + 10,000 - 25,000 = 230,000.

questions.question: The excess of a non-profit organization's assets over its liabilities (excluding accumulated fund adjustments) is generally referred to as the:
questions.explanation: The accumulated fund is the non-profit equivalent of capital, representing the excess of assets over liabilities built up over time.

questions.question: Entrance fees received by a club are usually treated, unless stated otherwise, as:
options: Income in the income and expenditure account
A direct addition to the accumulated fund only
questions.correct_answer: Income in the income and expenditure account
questions.explanation: Unless the constitution states they should be capitalized, entrance fees are normally treated as revenue income of the year received.

questions.question: In the absence of a partnership agreement, the Partnership Act provides that profits and losses are to be shared:
options: According to time devoted to the business
questions.explanation: Under general partnership law, in the absence of an agreement, partners share profits and losses equally regardless of capital contribution.

questions.question: A partnership is best defined as:
options: The relation between persons carrying on a business in common with a view to profit
A company registered under the Companies Act
questions.correct_answer: The relation between persons carrying on a business in common with a view to profit
questions.explanation: This is the standard legal definition of a partnership, distinguishing it from sole proprietorship and incorporated companies.

questions.question: In partnership accounts, each partner's capital and current accounts are usually kept:
options: Separately, to distinguish fixed capital from fluctuating items like drawings and share of profit
In the name of the senior partner only
Only for the partner with the highest capital
questions.correct_answer: Separately, to distinguish fixed capital from fluctuating items like drawings and share of profit
questions.explanation: Under the fixed capital method, capital accounts remain stable while drawings, interest, salaries, and profit shares pass through current accounts.

questions.question: Interest on partners' drawings, where charged, is treated in the appropriation account as a(n):
options: Addition to profit available for distribution
Deduction from profit available for distribution
Business expense in the profit and loss account
questions.correct_answer: Addition to profit available for distribution
questions.explanation: Interest on drawings is charged to partners and added back to the pool of profit to be shared, increasing the amount available for appropriation.

questions.question: Two partners, A and B, share profits equally. Net profit before appropriation is N400,000. A is entitled to a salary of N60,000. What is B's share of the residual profit?
questions.explanation: Residual profit after A's salary = 400,000 - 60,000 = 340,000, shared equally so each partner gets 170,000.

questions.question: A partnership appropriation account is used to show how:
options: Net profit is distributed among partners after salaries and interest
Cost of goods sold is determined
questions.correct_answer: Net profit is distributed among partners after salaries and interest
questions.explanation: The appropriation account allocates net profit to partners' salaries, interest on capital, interest on drawings, and the residual profit-sharing ratio.

questions.question: Departmental accounts are prepared mainly to:
options: Show the profitability of each department separately within one business
Replace the need for a trial balance
Comply with tax authority requirements only
Record transactions of different companies together
questions.correct_answer: Show the profitability of each department separately within one business
questions.explanation: Departmental accounts allocate revenues and costs to individual departments so management can assess each department's contribution to overall profit.

questions.question: In departmental accounts, expenses that cannot be directly traced to a single department (e.g. rent for a shared building) are usually apportioned using a:
options: Reasonable basis such as floor area or sales value
Random allocation decided by the cashier
Equal split regardless of department size
The most profitable department absorbing all costs
questions.correct_answer: Reasonable basis such as floor area or sales value
questions.explanation: Common apportionment bases include floor space (for rent/rates) or sales value (for selling expenses), chosen to reflect the benefit each department receives.

questions.question: A joint venture in accounting refers to:
options: A temporary business arrangement between two or more parties to undertake a specific venture and share profits or losses
A permanent partnership registered under CAMA
A sole proprietorship with multiple branches
questions.correct_answer: A temporary business arrangement between two or more parties to undertake a specific venture and share profits or losses
questions.explanation: A joint venture is typically a short-term collaboration for a specific project, after which the arrangement ends, distinguishing it from an ongoing partnership.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key difference between a joint venture and a partnership?
options: A joint venture is usually for a single transaction or limited period, while a partnership is an ongoing business
A joint venture must be registered while a partnership need not be
A partnership has no profit-sharing ratio
A joint venture always has more than five members
questions.correct_answer: A joint venture is usually for a single transaction or limited period, while a partnership is an ongoing business
questions.explanation: The temporary, project-specific nature of a joint venture is its key distinguishing feature from a continuing partnership.

questions.question: Which document is commonly used to record incomplete records transactions when a trader keeps only a cash book and lists of debtors/creditors?
questions.explanation: A statement of affairs lists known assets and liabilities to derive capital, forming the basis for preparing accounts from incomplete records.
